title: How is eighty nine written with the base five shapes?
description: A triangle is one, a square is five, a hexagon is twenty five and a circle is one hundred twenty five. The board takes the biggest shape that fits, then the next, until eighty nine is used up, and each count is checked by adding back. Keeko's doubt is that a long row of squares is a proper numeral.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a base five system each landmark is five of the one before, so take the biggest landmark that fits and never keep five of one shape. Watch for students who write many squares and a few triangles and stop there.

source: Write 89 in the base-5 system with triangle 1, square 5, hexagon 25 and circle 125.
video_script.why: The child writes a number in the book's base five system by taking the biggest landmark that fits first.
video_script.substitution: Take the biggest shape that fits as many times as it fits, then move to the next smaller shape.
video_script.anchor: the book's base five shapes: a triangle for one, a square for five, a hexagon for twenty five and a circle for one hundred twenty five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko stops at squares and triangles, giving a long row of seventeen squares; five squares make a hexagon, so the row must be regrouped
video_script.payoff_line: Eighty nine is three hexagons, two squares and four triangles.

final_answer.spoken: three hexagons, two squares and four triangles

maths_rules: triangle = 1, square = 5, hexagon = 25, circle = 125; each is 5 times the one before
2 x 5 = 10 and 3 x 5 = 15 > 14, so 2 squares; 14 - 10 = 4, so 4 triangles
Keeko's slip: 17 x 5 + 4 = 85 + 4 = 89, but 17 squares = 3 hexagons + 2 squares because 3 x 5 + 2 = 17
video_script.design: One idea: biggest landmark first, never five of a kind. The four shapes stay on the board; the numbers appear beside them in the working area.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the four shapes appear in a row with the numbers one, five, twenty five and one hundred twenty five beside them; then the number 89 with an empty box

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.shapes: the triangle, square and hexagon appear with their numbers
marks.ask: 89 appears with an empty box beside the shapes

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a number system made of shapes.
<bookmark mark='shapes'/>A triangle stands for one, a square for five, and a hexagon for twenty five.
<bookmark mark='circle'/>A circle stands for one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must write eighty nine using these shapes. How many of each shape do we need?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: five triangles slide into one square; five squares slide into one hexagon; five hexagons slide into one circle; the shapes line up from triangle to circle

marks.tri: five triangles slide together into one square
marks.sq: five squares slide into one hexagon, five hexagons into one circle
marks.land: the four values are circled as landmarks
marks.base: the words base five system appear under the row

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Five triangles are worth one square.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Five squares are worth one hexagon, and five hexagons are worth one circle.
<bookmark mark='land'/>The values one, five, twenty five and one hundred twenty five are called landmark numbers.
<bookmark mark='base'/>When each landmark is five times the one before, we call it a base five system.

beats.on_screen: Given: triangle 1, square 5, hexagon 25, circle 125; number 89

marks.given: the four values and the number 89 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a triangle is one, a square is five, and a hexagon is twenty five. A circle is one hundred twenty five. The number is eighty nine.

marks.find: the words 89 in shapes are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write eighty nine using these shapes.

beats.on_screen: Start with the biggest landmark that fits: circle 125 > 89, cross it out; hexagon 25 fits

marks.big: the rule Start with the biggest landmark that fits is written
marks.skip: the circle is crossed out and the hexagon is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step one, start with the biggest landmark that fits.
<bookmark mark='skip'/>A circle is one hundred twenty five, which is more than eighty nine, so we skip it. A hexagon is twenty five, and that fits.

marks.hex: three hexagons and the line 3 x 25 = 75 appear

narration: <bookmark mark='hex'/>Step two, count the hexagons. Three times twenty five is seventy five, and four would be a hundred, which is too many.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Eighty nine take away seventy five leaves fourteen.

beats.on_screen: 2 x 5 = 10 (3 x 5 = 15 is too big); 14 - 10 = 4, so 4 triangles

marks.sq: two squares and the line 2 x 5 = 10 appear
marks.tri: four triangles appear for the last four

narration: <bookmark mark='sq'/>Step three, count the squares. Two times five is ten, and three would be fifteen, which is too many.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Fourteen take away ten leaves four.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Each triangle is one, so the last four are four triangles.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding the parts back. Seventy five plus ten plus four is eighty nine, which is the number we started with.

marks.ans: the three hexagons, two squares and four triangles are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Eighty nine is three hexagons, two squares and four triangles.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished numeral
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's row of 17 squares and 4 triangles; five squares at a time circled and slid into hexagons; the row becomes 3 hexagons and 2 squares

marks.doubt: a long row of seventeen squares and four triangles appears
marks.five: groups of five squares are circled and slide into hexagons
marks.fix: the row becomes three hexagons, two squares and the four triangles

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is seventeen squares and four triangles. Seventeen times five is eighty five, and four more is eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The total is right, but every five squares are worth one hexagon.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Seventeen squares become three hexagons and two squares, and we never keep five of one shape.
